Quadratic Functions

title: Algebra II Notes
text:
A quadratic function is a function that can be written in the form
\[
f(x)=ax^2+bx+c
\]
where
\[
a \neq 0.
\]
The graph of a quadratic function is called a parabola.



The standard form of a quadratic function is
\[
f(x)=ax^2+bx+c.
\]
For example,
\[
f(x)=2x^2-4x-6.
\]
In this function,
\[
a=2,\qquad b=-4,\qquad c=-6.
\]


The value of \(a\) determines the direction and width of the parabola.

If \(a>0\), the parabola opens upward.
If \(a<0\), the parabola opens downward.
Larger values of \(|a|\) make the parabola narrower.
Smaller values of \(|a|\) make the parabola wider.







TipQuick Check



For
\[
f(x)=-3x^2+5x+2,
\]
the parabola opens downward because
\[
a=-3<0.
\]

title: Algebra II Notes
text:
Example
Find the vertex of
\[
f(x)=x^2-6x+5.
\]
Here,
\[
a=1,\qquad b=-6.
\]
Use the vertex formula:
\[
x=\frac{-(-6)}{2(1)}
\]
\[
x=\frac{6}{2}
\]
\[
x=3.
\]
Now substitute \(x=3\) into the function:
\[
f(3)=3^2-6(3)+5
\]
\[
f(3)=9-18+5
\]
\[
f(3)=-4.
\]
Therefore, the vertex is
\[
\boxed{(3,-4)}.
\]

title: Algebra II Notes
text:
Example
Solve
\[
2x^2+3x-2=0.
\]
Identify the coefficients:
\[
a=2,\qquad b=3,\qquad c=-2.
\]
Substitute into the formula:
\[
x=
\frac{-3\pm\sqrt{3^2-4(2)(-2)}}{2(2)}.
\]
Simplify:
\[
x=
\frac{-3\pm\sqrt{9+16}}{4}.
\]
\[
x=
\frac{-3\pm\sqrt{25}}{4}.
\]
\[
x=
\frac{-3\pm5}{4}.
\]
This gives two solutions:
\[
x=\frac{-3+5}{4}=\frac12
\]
and
\[
x=\frac{-3-5}{4}=-2.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\boxed{x=\frac12 \text{ or } x=-2}.
\]

title: Algebra II Notes
text:
Example
Consider
\[
x^2+4x+8=0.
\]
The discriminant is
\[
b^2-4ac.
\]
Substitute:
\[
4^2-4(1)(8)
\]
\[
16-32=-16.
\]
Since
\[
-16<0,
\]
the equation has no real solutions.
